evidence: The mechanics are as described: process_inbox_pr_review is @shared_task(max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5) (tasks.py:1109), commits a QUEUED ReviewRun (tasks.py:1223-1230), starts the workflow in transaction.on_commit (tasks.py:1234), and routes a start failure into .retry() (tasks.py:1235-1237); no stale-QUEUED sweeper exists (schedules.py only wires the daily digest). But this is the same deliberate design the pre-existing webhook path already uses, with identical max_retries=3 and the same 'retry re-enters and restarts the still-QUEUED run' recovery (tasks.py:809, 1001-1013, 1069-1076), so the PR copies an established pattern rather than introducing a defect. Each Celery attempt also absorbs SDK-level gRPC retries (execute_stamphog_review_workflow uses async_connect() with default RetryConfig, temporal/client.py:42-55), and a stranded QUEUED row never blocks anything: the receiver re-fires on every later TaskRun output save (receivers.py:72-139; saves recur via set_task_run_output at tasks/facade/api.py:2138-2154 and _record_run_output_field at webhooks.py:279-295) and the inbox dedupe restarts a QUEUED run at the current head (tasks.py:1195-1214, covered by test_tasks.py:992-1021), while any later webhook supersedes it via _supersede_prior_runs (tasks.py:415-432). Each failed attempt is logged with logger.exception and Celery logs MaxRetriesExceededError, so it is not silent to operators. What remains is an operational-hardening ask (reconciliation task, metric, alert) for a Temporal outage longer than the roughly one-minute combined retry window at the moment an inbox PR is recorded, which is a defensive enhancement, not a correctness defect in this PR.
notes: I would change my mind if production data showed Temporal start outages routinely exceed the combined Celery+SDK retry window, or if the webhook path had a reconciliation mechanism that the new inbox path lacks.
